overview: Separately catalogued skulls, limb bones and teeth support an aquatic-wading interpretation and a raoellid sister placement to Cetacea in the published analysis.

ecology.diet: Diet unresolved; stable isotopes constrain water use more directly than food choice
ecology.habitat: Aquatic or riparian use inferred from bone density and isotopes
ecology.locomotion: Wading interpretation inferred; no associated skeleton preserves a complete gait
ecology.guild: Aquatic-wading ecological interpretation with diet unresolved

evidenceSummary: The material is a disarticulated bone-bed sample, not one skeleton; aquatic ecology and sister placement are inferences, and Indohyus is neither crown Cetacea nor a demonstrated ancestor.

overview: Partial skeleton H-GSP 18507 combines large weight-bearing limbs with vertebral and hind-limb anatomy used to model amphibious swimming.

ecology.diet: Aquatic predation inferred from teeth and skull; prey not directly observed
ecology.habitat: Amphibious use inferred from anatomy and formation context
ecology.locomotion: Dorsoventral swimming and land movement are functional models
ecology.bodySize: Large-bodied early cetacean represented by a partial skeleton

traits: Substantial weight-bearing fore- and hind limbs
Vertebral and limb mosaic used in locomotor comparison
evidenceSummary: The holotype directly records an amphibious anatomical mosaic; otter-like swimming and sea-lion-like land movement are analogue-based models, not observed behaviour or ancestry.

overview: Holotype CGM 60584 combines a long posterior trunk, unfused sacrals, no weight-bearing sacroiliac joint and reduced limbs in a model of increasing tail propulsion.

ecology.diet: Marine predation inferred from cetacean dentition; prey not directly preserved
ecology.locomotion: Mid-body and tail undulation inferred; tail fluke not preserved
ecology.bodySize: Large protocetid represented by substantial associated remains

traits: Unfused sacrals without a weight-bearing sacroiliac joint
Reduced limbs and no securely preserved tail fluke
evidenceSummary: Associated material documents the locomotor anatomy, but age placement straddles competing stratigraphic interpretations and tail-driven swimming remains a model rather than observed performance.

commonNameZh: 地点组合的陆生早期鲸
geography: H-GSP Locality 62, Ganda Kas, Kala Chitta Hills, Punjab, Pakistan
overview: Thewissen et al. report a wolf-sized Pakicetus attocki reconstruction from separately catalogued early-Eocene material at one Pakistani site; cranial and postcranial anatomy supports a terrestrial locomotor interpretation.

ecology.diet: Diet is unresolved from the described skeleton and teeth; the study does not attribute prey remains to the sample
ecology.habitat: Terrestrial use is inferred from the locomotor skeleton; the locality and formation do not prove a shoreline microhabitat
ecology.locomotion: Running and terrestrial locomotion are inferred from limb proportions and osteology; performance was not observed
ecology.bodySize: Wolf-sized pakicetid in the authors' comparison
ecology.guild: Terrestrial early-cetacean interpretation with ecological guild bounded to the named sample

traits: Cetacean-like basicranial ear region in skull H-GSP 96231
Weight-bearing limbs and running adaptations in separately catalogued postcrania
evidenceSummary: Skull H-GSP 96231 and separately catalogued vertebrae and limb bones from H-GSP Locality 62 support a terrestrial body plan, but the reconstruction is not one associated skeleton and Pakicetus is not presented as a direct ancestor.

geography: Lowest Yumaque Member, Paracas Formation, Playa Media Luna, Pisco Basin, Peru
overview: Holotype MUSM 3580 is a partial skeleton from the middle Eocene Yumaque Member of coastal Peru; its sacral attachment, robust limbs and hoof-like phalanges document a quadrupedal whale with both aquatic and weight-bearing anatomical signals.

ecology.diet: Carnivory is inferred from cetacean dentition; prey and feeding behaviour are not preserved
ecology.habitat: Marine depositional context is documented, while amphibious habitat use is inferred from the skeleton
ecology.locomotion: Quadrupedal swimming and terrestrial weight bearing are functional reconstructions; no gait or swimming performance was observed
ecology.bodySize: Approximately 4 m long according to the reported skeletal dimensions
ecology.guild: Amphibious quadrupedal cetacean interpretation with route and behaviour unresolved

traits: Partial articulated holotype MUSM 3580 preserving mandibles and most major postcranial regions
Two fused sacrals, defined femoral head and hoof-like distal phalanges
Functional hind limbs alongside aquatic cetacean adaptations
evidenceSummary: MUSM 3580 fixes an approximately 42.6 Ma Peruvian protocetid occurrence and preserves anatomy consistent with weight bearing and aquatic locomotion; walking, swimming and westward dispersal remain analytical interpretations, not direct ancestry.
